title: Modularize local runner into lightweight shim; add path-aware cache hints and fail-fast staging lane
author: Asha Raman
release_notes: Introduce a modular local runner shim and path-aware cache hints; add a fail-fast staging lane to surface infra issues earlier. Expect CI median PR runtimes to drop ~65% and local iterative loops to be significantly faster.
description:
Context and motivation: our monolithic build-hook and the single 'run-all' local helper are slowing down iterative development and bloating CI images. Flaky CI runs are often caused by unnecessary full-workspace build steps and broad cache invalidation. This PR replaces the legacy monolithic scripts with a small, well-documented local-runner shim that composes modular task runners, and it adds path-aware cache hints so GH Actions only warms caches relevant to touched packages. It also introduces a fail-fast 'staging' lane that runs a targeted smoke+infra check early in the pipeline to catch cloud infra regressions before heavy integration tests.

What changed (high level):
- Introduced cmd/local-runner (shim in Go) that discovers and runs per-package task runners with minimal startup overhead.
- Converted the legacy scripts/ci-run.sh and scripts/dev-loop.sh into small adapters that call the shim.
- Added .github/actions/cache-hints composite action which computes cache keys based on touched paths and emits explicit cache-hint metadata for downstream steps.
- Added a new workflow .github/workflows/staging-smoke.yml (fast-fail lane) that executes in ~3m and gates the heavier lanes.
- Pipeline updates: split integration jobs into 'smoke', 'integration-heavy', and 'on-demand' to improve parallelism and reduce wasted work.
- Updated docs/dev/LOCAL_RUNNER.md and added examples under examples/runner-configs/ for common dev loops.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1984/local-runner-modularization (attached)
- [x] Unit tests for the shim and cache-hints action
- [x] Migration guide in docs/dev/LOCAL_RUNNER.md
- [x] Verified upstream CI runtimes on sample repos (see metrics below)

Metrics observed in canary (summary):
- Median PR CI runtime on sample subset: reduced from 19m -> 6.5m (approx 66% improvement)
- Cache hit rate for node deps increased from 72% -> 91% on canary runs due to targeted keys
- Local iterative edit->test time reduced from ~45s to ~12s for common TS package changes

Rollout plan: staged rollout over 2 weeks. Default workflows remain until rollout flag flips in .github/rollout-config. We will keep the legacy scripts for one release as adapters and then deprecate them after internal teams confirm no blockers.

Notes on compatibility: no breaking changes to public SDKs or published artifacts. Local runner uses the same environment variables as prior scripts; where behavior differs we document fallbacks.

Related work: ENG-2045 (ci-stage-lanes), several prior CI refactors informed the design: PRs in 2024-2025 that split integration tests and added cache heuristics.

Next steps: follow-up PR to add granular cache warming for Python wheels and to wire the runner into the ephemeral CI runners workflow for cost savings.
